overall: Violations found: improper executive sessions on the development agreement, insufficiently detailed executive session notices, and an undisclosed anticipated topic on the February 10 notice; no unposted deliberation; minutes ordered released.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly held executive sessions on a development agreement for a 40B project, a subject outside any statutory executive session purpose.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board’s November 4, 2019, December 16, 2019, January 21, 2020, February 3, 2020, and February 10, 2020, discussions did not fall within a statutory purpose for executive session, and must be released in their entirety.

allegations.summary: Executive session notices for the development agreement discussions allegedly did not identify the property or nature of the discussion.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board has failed to meet its burden of demonstrating how disclosing the nature of the discussion, or identifying the real property to be discussed, would have compromised a valid purpose for the executive sessions.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly met in an unposted meeting to approve the development agreement before its February 10 vote.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find no violation of the Open Meeting Law regarding improper deliberation outside of a meeting by the Board.

allegations.summary: The February 10, 2020 notice allegedly omitted anticipated topics, including the development agreement and related warrant articles, that were discussed.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing anticipated topics without including them on the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged the AG to find the violations intentional; the Board claimed good-faith reliance on counsel's advice.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to find an intentional violation here.

allegations.summary: Allegation that the Board lacked authority to create a proposed redevelopment agency and lease space in the development.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, these allegations would not constitute violations of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

allegations.summary: Allegation that the development agreement was left out of the meeting packet for the February 20, 2020 Board meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, these allegations would not constitute violations of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

allegations.summary: Allegation of deliberation outside a meeting in preparing to retain special counsel for the development agreement, which the AG found untimely.
allegations.key_passage: However, as the retention of special counsel was disclosed during an open session on December 16, 2019, we find this allegation to be untimely and decline to review it.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.

Release the portions of the November 4, 2019, December 16, 2019, January 21, 2020, February 3, 2020, and February 10, 2020 executive session minutes that relate to the development agreement within 30 days of receipt of the order.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
